answer: The raven multiplier is published, charged in garden, and river lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4740 identities would post 2867 proofs and burn roughly 6 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
